name: after
synopsis:

after cancel id
after cancel script ?script ...?
after idle ?options? script ?script ...?
after info ?id?
after active
after clear
after counts
after dump
after enable ?enabled?
after flags ?flags?
description: Execute a command after a time delay
examples:
# Schedule a command to run in 1 second
after 1000 {puts "Hello, World!"}

# Sleep for 500 milliseconds
after 500

# Cancel a scheduled event
set id [after 5000 {puts "This won't print"}]
after cancel $id

# Schedule an idle callback
after idle {puts "Event loop is idle"}

# List all pending events
after info

name: apply
examples:
# Apply a simple lambda
apply {{x y} {expr {$x + $y}}} 3 4
# Returns: 7

# Lambda with default arguments
apply {{x {y 10}} {expr {$x + $y}}} 5
# Returns: 15

# Lambda with namespace
apply {{x} {variable myVar; return "$myVar: $x"} ::myns} "test"

# Using apply with lmap
lmap x {1 2 3 4 5} {apply {{n} {expr {$n * $n}}} $x}
# Returns: 1 4 9 16 25

name: expr
examples:
Basic arithmetic:

        
expr {2 + 3}        ;# 5
expr {10 / 3}       ;# 3 (integer division)
expr {10.0 / 3}     ;# 3.333...
expr {10 % 3}       ;# 1
expr {2 ** 10}      ;# 1024


        
Comparisons:

        
expr {5 > 3}        ;# 1 (true)
expr {5 == 5}       ;# 1
expr {"abc" eq "abc"}  ;# 1
expr {"x" in {a b x}}  ;# 1


        
Logical operations:

        
expr {1 && 0}       ;# 0
expr {1 || 0}       ;# 1
expr {!0}           ;# 1


        
Ternary conditional:

        
set x 5
expr {$x > 0 ? "positive" : "non-positive"}


        
Math functions:

        
expr {sqrt(16)}     ;# 4.0
expr {sin(3.14159/2)}  ;# ~1.0
expr {max(1, 5, 3)} ;# 5
expr {round(3.7)}   ;# 4


        
Using variables (brace for safety):

        
set a 10
set b 20
expr {$a + $b}      ;# 30

name: file
examples:
Path manipulation:

        
# Split and join paths
set path "/home/user/documents/file.txt"
puts [file dirname $path]    ;# /home/user/documents
puts [file tail $path]       ;# file.txt
puts [file extension $path]  ;# .txt
puts [file rootname $path]   ;# /home/user/documents/file

# Join path components
set newpath [file join /home user documents]
puts $newpath  ;# /home/user/documents

# Normalize path
puts [file normalize "./test/../file.txt"]


        
File tests:

        
if {[file exists $filename]} {
    if {[file isfile $filename]} {
        puts "Size: [file size $filename] bytes"
    } elseif {[file isdirectory $filename]} {
        puts "It's a directory"
    }
}

if {[file readable $filename] && [file writable $filename]} {
    puts "File is readable and writable"
}


        
File information:

        
# Get file statistics
file stat $filename info
puts "Size: $info(size)"
puts "Modified: [clock format $info(mtime)]"
puts "Type: $info(type)"

# Get specific times
puts "Access time: [clock format [file atime $filename]]"
puts "Modify time: [clock format [file mtime $filename]]"


        
File operations:

        
# Create directory
file mkdir /tmp/myapp/data

# Copy file
file copy source.txt destination.txt
file copy -force source.txt destination.txt  ;# overwrite

# Rename/move
file rename oldname.txt newname.txt

# Delete
file delete temp.txt
file delete -force /tmp/myapp  ;# recursive delete


        
Temporary files:

        
# Get temp directory
set tmpdir [file temppath]
puts "Temp dir: $tmpdir"

# Get unique temp filename
set tmpfile [file tempname]
puts "Temp file: $tmpfile"

name: interp
examples:
Create and use a child interpreter:

        
# Create a child interpreter
interp create child

# Evaluate code in the child
interp eval child {
    set x 10
    proc double {n} { expr {$n * 2} }
}

# Call a procedure in the child
set result [interp eval child {double $x}]
puts $result  ;# 20

# Delete the child
interp delete child


        
Create a safe interpreter:

        
# Create a safe (sandboxed) interpreter
interp create -safe sandbox

# Verify it's safe
puts [interp issafe sandbox]  ;# 1

# Safe interpreters have restricted access
# file, exec, socket, load, etc. are hidden or removed

interp delete sandbox


        
Create aliases:

        
interp create child

# Create an alias - 'myPuts' in child calls 'puts' in parent
interp alias child myPuts {} puts

# Now child can use myPuts
interp eval child {myPuts "Hello from child!"}

# Create alias with preset arguments
interp alias child sayHello {} puts "Hello,"
interp eval child {sayHello "World"}  ;# Hello, World

interp delete child


        
Set resource limits:

        
interp create limited

# Set a recursion limit to prevent infinite recursion
interp recursionlimit limited 50

# Set an execution limit
interp execlimit limited 10000

# Try to exceed limits (will error)
catch {
    interp eval limited {
        proc bomb {} { bomb }
        bomb
    }
} err
puts "Error: $err"

interp delete limited


        
Hide and expose commands:

        
interp create child

# Hide the 'file' command
interp hide child file

# 'file' is now inaccessible normally
catch {interp eval child {file exists /tmp}} err
puts $err  ;# invalid command name "file"

# But can be invoked via invokehidden
interp invokehidden child file exists /tmp

# Re-expose it
interp expose child file

interp delete child

# Append text using invoke
object invoke $sb Append ", World!"

# Get the result
set result [object invoke $sb ToString]
puts $result  ;# Output: Hello, World!

# Dispose the object
object dispose $sb


        
Create with alias for easier access:

        
# Create with -alias option
set sb [object create -alias System.Text.StringBuilder]

# Now you can use the alias directly
$sb Append "Hello"
$sb Append " World"
puts [$sb ToString]

# Clean up
object dispose $sb


        
Call static methods:

        
# Call a static method on System.IO.Path
set fullPath [object invoke System.IO.Path GetFullPath "myfile.txt"]

# Get environment variable via System.Environment
set home [object invoke System.Environment GetEnvironmentVariable "HOME"]


        
Work with collections:

        
# Create an ArrayList
set list [object create System.Collections.ArrayList]
object invoke $list Add "one"
object invoke $list Add "two"
object invoke $list Add "three"

# Iterate over it
object foreach item $list {
    puts "Item: $item"
}

# Use lmap to transform
set upper [object lmap item $list {
    string toupper $item
}]

object dispose $list


        
Load and use an assembly:

        
# Load an assembly
object load System.Xml

# Create an XmlDocument
set doc [object create System.Xml.XmlDocument]
object invoke $doc LoadXml "
test
"

# Query the document
set node [object invoke $doc SelectSingleNode "/root/item"]
puts [object invoke $node InnerText]

object dispose $doc


        
List available members:

        
# Get members of a type
set members [object members System.String]
puts $members

# Get methods only
set methods [object members -membertypes Method System.String]


        
Type checking:

        
set list [object create System.Collections.ArrayList]

# Check type
puts [object isoftype $list System.Collections.IList]  ;# 1
puts [object isoftype $list System.String]              ;# 0

# Check if null or disposed
puts [object isnull $list]      ;# 0
puts [object isdisposed $list]  ;# 0

object dispose $list
puts [object isdisposed $list]  ;# 1

name: package
synopsis:
package absent ?-exact? package ?version?
package alias ?options? name ?package? ?version?
package aliases ?pattern?
package forget ?package package ...?
package ifneeded package version ?script? ?flags?
package indexes ?pattern?
package info name
package loaded ?pattern?

package vcompare version1 version2
package versions package
package vloaded ?pattern?
package vsatisfies version1 version2
package vsort versionList
package withdraw package ?version?
description: Facilities for package loading and version management
examples:
Require a package:

        
# Load a package (any version)
package require http

# Load a specific minimum version
package require http 2.0

# Load an exact version
package require -exact http 2.7.0


        
Provide a package:

        
# At the end of your package script:
package provide mypackage 1.0


        
Check if a package is loaded:

        
# Check without loading
if {![catch {package present http}]} {
    puts "http package is already loaded"
}

# Get version of loaded package
set ver [package provide http]
if {$ver ne ""} {
    puts "http version $ver is loaded"
}


        
Register a package:

        
# Register how to load a package
package ifneeded mypackage 1.0 {
    source /path/to/mypackage.eagle
}

# See what script is registered
puts [package ifneeded mypackage 1.0]


        
List packages:

        
# List all known packages
puts [package names]

# List all versions of a package
puts [package versions http]

# List loaded packages
puts [package loaded]


        
Version comparison:

        
# Compare versions
puts [package vcompare 1.0 2.0]    ;# -1
puts [package vcompare 2.0 2.0]    ;# 0
puts [package vcompare 2.1 2.0]    ;# 1

# Check if version satisfies requirement
puts [package vsatisfies 2.1 2.0]  ;# 1
puts [package vsatisfies 1.9 2.0]  ;# 0


        
Create a package alias:

        
# Make "myhttp" load "http" package
package alias myhttp http 2.0

# Now this will load http:
package require myhttp


        
Scan for packages:

        
# Scan auto_path for packages
package scan

# Scan specific directories
package scan /opt/tcl/lib /usr/local/lib/tcl

set result [regexp -inline {(\d+)-(\d+)-(\d+)} "Date: 2024-01-15"]

Using -all:

        
regexp -all {\d+} "a1b2c3d4"  ;# 4


        
Using -indices:

Case-insensitive:
